If both of <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> are universal homeomorphisms, so is <MATH_0003> by
Lemma <REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Suppose both of <MATH_0004> and <MATH_0005> are universal homeomorphisms. We want to show
that <MATH_0006> is also. Now base change the diagram along an arbitrary morphism
<MATH_0007> of schemes,  we get the following diagram with all
squares Cartesian:
<MATH_0008>
Our assumption implies that the composition <MATH_0009>
and <MATH_0010> are homeomorphisms, therefore so is <MATH_0011>.
This finishes the proof of <MATH_0012> being a universal homeomorphism.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Finally, assume <MATH_0013> and <MATH_0014> are universal
homeomorphisms. We want to show that <MATH_0015> is a universal homeomorphism.
Let <MATH_0016> be an arbitrary morphism of schemes.
We get the following diagram with all squares Cartesian:
<MATH_0017>
Here the morphism <MATH_0018> is defined by the universal property of
fiber products and the two morphisms
<MATH_0019> and <MATH_0020>.
We shall prove that <MATH_0021> is a homeomorphism.
Since the property of being a homeomorphism has 2-out-of-3 property, we see
that <MATH_0022> is a homeomorphism.
Staring at the top square, it suffices to prove that <MATH_0023> is a universal
homeomorphism. Since <MATH_0024> is a homeomorphism, we see that it is
an affine morphism by Lemma <REF_0002>
and a fortiori separated (Lemma <REF_0003>).
Since <MATH_0025> is the identity, we see that <MATH_0026>
is a closed immersion by
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0004>.
Since <MATH_0027> is bijective, it follows that <MATH_0028> is a bijective
closed immersion and hence a universal homeomorphism (for example by the
characterization in Lemma <REF_0005>) as desired.
